evals.name: fresh-clone-bringup
evals.prompt: I just cloned this digital-signage repo onto a fresh NUC with an Intel iGPU. Docker's installed and that's about it. Walk me through everything I need to do to get the demo actually running in a browser — I've never deployed this before and I'd rather not discover a missing step three hours in.
evals.expected_output: An ordered bring-up procedure covering: model download (all three models), setting the two empty MTX WebRTC credentials in .env with their validation rules, HOST_IP guidance, make build && make up, verification, and the correct URL https://localhost:5000 over HTTPS with a self-signed-cert warning.
assertions: States that MTX_WEBRTCICESERVERS2_0_USERNAME and MTX_WEBRTCICESERVERS2_0_PASSWORD ship empty and must be set before make up will succeed
Gives the actual validation rules for those credentials (username letters-only min 5; password alphanumeric min 8 with at least one digit)
Covers downloading all three models (YOLO11s detection, SDXL-Turbo, MiniLM embeddings) before make up
Gives the access URL as https on port 5000 (not http) and mentions the self-signed certificate warning
Presents the steps in a workable order with model download and .env config before make up

evals.name: black-video-stuck-ad
evals.prompt: ok so the stack is up, all containers running, and I can load the web ui from my laptop at https://192.168.1.50:5000 — but the video area is just black and the ad panel is stuck showing the same image forever. worked fine when i was testing on the machine itself. what's going on
evals.expected_output: Identifies HOST_IP still being localhost (or otherwise wrong) as the likely root cause of the black video for a remote browser, because HOST_IP is interpolated into the TURN URL handed to the browser. Separately explains the stuck ad panel, including the 204 No Content polling semantics.
assertions: Identifies HOST_IP as the likely cause of the black video and explains it is substituted into the TURN/ICE server URL given to the browser
Notes that the symptom appearing only for a remote browser (worked locally) is the diagnostic signal for HOST_IP=localhost
Addresses the stuck ad panel as a separate issue rather than assuming one root cause explains both
Mentions concrete diagnostic commands or log checks rather than only offering speculation
States that .env changes require make up (not docker restart) to take effect

evals.name: npu-and-rtsp-camera
evals.prompt: two changes i need to make: run the object detection on the NPU instead of CPU, and stop using the sample video — point it at our RTSP camera at 10.0.0.42 (creds are viewer/viewer123, path is /stream1). tell me exactly what to edit.
evals.expected_output: Names configs/pid/config.json for both changes: the device field under payload.parameters.detection-properties, and the pipeline string's source element replaced with rtspsrc plus rtph264depay. Distinguishes detection device from AIG_MODEL_DEVICE.
assertions: Names configs/pid/config.json as the file to edit for BOTH the device change and the RTSP source change
Sets the detection device via the payload parameters detection-properties device field, not via an environment variable
Provides an rtspsrc pipeline that includes rtph264depay before h264parse
Distinguishes the detection device from the AIG/SDXL generation device (AIG_MODEL_DEVICE) rather than conflating them
Mentions the NPU requires /dev/accel on the host, or otherwise flags the device-availability prerequisite
